question.text: Consider an object undergoing rectilinear motion with constant acceleration. At instant t = 0, its velocity equals v₁, while at instant t = t, its velocity reaches v₂. The claim states that its mean velocity over this duration is (v₁ + v₂)/2. State whether this statement is true or false.
conditions: velocity at t = t is v₂

solution.approach: For uniform acceleration, velocity is a linear function of time, so its average over any interval equals the average of the endpoint values.

steps.text: Write velocity as a linear function of time for uniform acceleration.
Average velocity over 0 to t is the mean value of this linear function.
Since v₂ = v₁ + at, substitute at = v₂ − v₁ into the average. This gives the stated formula, so the statement is true.
